questions.stem: Republic Act No. 6713 is also known as the:
choices: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
questions.explanation: Section 1 of RA 6713 gives its title as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. The Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act is RA 3019.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees shall lead modest lives and uphold:
choices: the interest of their political party
loyalty to their superiors above all
questions.explanation: The declaration of policy in Section 2 requires public officials and employees to lead modest lives and uphold public interest over personal interest.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, the term "public officials" includes employees who are:
choices: receiving at least the minimum wage
permanent or temporary, whether or not they receive compensation
questions.explanation: Section 3(b) covers elective and appointive officials and employees, permanent or temporary, career or non-career, including military and police personnel, whether or not they receive compensation, regardless of amount.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, which of the following is NOT considered a "gift"?
choices: A free trip offered by a contractor with a pending bid
A simulated sale in favor of the official
An unsolicited gift of nominal value not given in exchange for a favor
Cash given in anticipation of a favor
questions.explanation: Section 3(c) excludes an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor.

questions.stem: For purposes of RA 6713, the "family" of a public official or employee means their:
choices: relatives within the fourth civil degree
spouse and unmarried children under eighteen years of age
questions.explanation: Section 3(g) defines the family of public officials or employees as their spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, "relatives" refers to persons related to a public official within what degree of consanguinity or affinity?
questions.explanation: Section 3(k) defines relatives as persons related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity, including bilas, inso and balae.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, a "conflict of interest" arises when an official's interest in a private corporation or business:
choices: earns more than the official's salary
is registered under the official's spouse
may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty
questions.explanation: Section 3(i) says conflict of interest arises when the interest of the corporation or business, or the official's rights or duties in it, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty.

questions.stem: "Divestment" under RA 6713 is the transfer of title or disposal of interest in property in favor of a person other than:
questions.explanation: Section 3(j) requires divestment to be in favor of a person or persons other than the official's spouse and relatives; transferring to them does not count.

questions.stem: Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 requires officials to use government resources efficiently, effectively, honestly and economically to avoid wastage of public funds?
questions.explanation: Under Section 4(A)(a), commitment to public interest includes using government resources and powers efficiently, effectively, honestly and economically, particularly to avoid wastage in public funds and revenues.

questions.stem: Which norm of conduct requires public officials to perform their duties with the highest degree of excellence, intelligence and skill?
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(b), Professionalism, requires performing duties with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence and skill.

questions.stem: Under the norm of justness and sincerity, officials shall not discriminate against anyone, especially:
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(c) requires officials to act with justness and sincerity and not discriminate against anyone, especially the poor and the underprivileged.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, officials may extend favors to relatives on account of their office ONLY with respect to appointments to positions that are:
choices: strictly confidential or personal staff coterminous with the official
vacant for more than a year
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(c) bars undue favors to relatives, except appointments to positions considered strictly confidential or as members of personal staff whose terms are coterminous with the official's.

questions.stem: A government clerk serves all clients equally regardless of the clients' party affiliation. This reflects which norm of conduct?
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(d), Political neutrality, requires service to everyone without unfair discrimination and regardless of party affiliation or preference.

questions.stem: Extending prompt, courteous, and adequate service to the public and avoiding red tape falls under which norm of conduct?
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(e), Responsiveness to the public, requires prompt, courteous, and adequate service, openness of information, and avoiding red tape.

questions.stem: Promoting the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology is part of which norm of conduct?
questions.explanation: Under Section 4(A)(f), Nationalism and patriotism includes loyalty to the Republic and promoting the use of locally produced goods, resources and technology.

questions.stem: Under the norm of commitment to democracy, public officials shall put loyalty to country above loyalty to:
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(g) requires officials to uphold the Constitution and put loyalty to country above loyalty to persons or party.

questions.stem: A public employee who avoids extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth is observing which norm of conduct?
questions.explanation: Section 4(A)(h), Simple living, requires officials and their families to lead modest lives and not indulge in extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, within how many working days must public officials respond to letters and other communications sent by the public?
questions.explanation: Section 5(a) requires a response within fifteen (15) working days from receipt, and the reply must contain the action taken on the request.

questions.stem: Heads of government offices must render an annual performance report within how many working days from the end of the year?
questions.explanation: Section 5(b) requires heads of offices and agencies to render a performance report within forty-five (45) working days from the end of the year.

questions.stem: As far as practicable, official papers and documents should contain not more than how many signatories?
questions.explanation: Section 5(c) states that official documents must contain, as far as practicable, not more than three (3) signatories.

questions.stem: Who co-chair the Committee on Awards to Outstanding Public Officials and Employees under RA 6713?
choices: The President and the Senate President
The Ombudsman and the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission
The Chief Justice and the Ombudsman
The Chairman of the Commission on Audit and the Executive Secretary
questions.explanation: Section 6 creates the Committee with the Ombudsman and the CSC Chairman as Co-Chairmen, and the COA Chairman and two presidential appointees as members.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, public officials shall not have any financial or material interest in any transaction:
choices: requiring the approval of their office
questions.explanation: Section 7(a) prohibits any direct or indirect financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office.

questions.stem: The prohibitions on outside employment under Section 7(b) of RA 6713 continue to apply for how long after resignation, retirement, or separation from office?
questions.explanation: Section 7(b) extends these prohibitions for a period of one (1) year after resignation, retirement, or separation from public office.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prohibited act under Section 7(b) of RA 6713?
choices: Owning a home in the province
Recommending a person to a private company that has a pending transaction with one's office
Attending a public seminar on ethics
Teaching part-time with the agency head's permission where allowed by law
questions.explanation: Section 7(b)(3) prohibits recommending any person to any position in a private enterprise which has a regular or pending official transaction with the official's office.

questions.stem: Using confidential information known by reason of one's office to give undue advantage to anyone is prohibited under RA 6713 as:
choices: disclosure and/or misuse of confidential information
questions.explanation: Section 7(c) prohibits using or divulging confidential or classified information officially known by reason of office to further private interests, give undue advantage to anyone, or prejudice the public interest.

questions.stem: Regarding gifts from foreign governments, Congress consents to a public official's acceptance of all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Travel grants for travel entirely outside the Philippines, if permitted by the head of office
A scholarship or fellowship grant or medical treatment
A gift of nominal value received as a souvenir or mark of courtesy
Cash gifts of any amount given as tokens of friendship
questions.explanation: Section 7(d) lists only the three consented cases: nominal-value souvenirs, scholarship/fellowship grants or medical treatment, and appropriate travel grants outside the Philippines permitted by the head of office.

questions.stem: Who among the following is NOT required to file a Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) under RA 6713?
questions.explanation: Section 8(A) exempts those who serve in an honorary capacity, laborers, and casual or temporary workers.

questions.stem: After the first filing, the SALN must be filed on or before what date every year?
questions.explanation: Section 8(A) requires filing within thirty days after assumption of office, on or before April 30 of every year thereafter, and within thirty days after separation from the service.

questions.stem: A newly appointed employee must file their SALN within how many days after assumption of office?
questions.explanation: Section 8(A) requires the SALN to be filed within thirty (30) days after assumption of office.

questions.stem: Husband and wife who are both public employees may file their SALN:
choices: only through the head of office
questions.explanation: Section 8(A) provides that husband and wife who are both public officials or employees may file the required statements jointly or separately.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, how long must statements filed under the Act be available to the public?
questions.explanation: Section 8(C)(4) keeps statements available to the public for ten (10) years after receipt, after which they may be destroyed unless needed in an ongoing investigation.

questions.stem: When a conflict of interest arises, an official must divest themselves of shareholdings or interest within how many days from assumption of office?
questions.explanation: Section 9 requires resigning from the private business within thirty (30) days and/or divesting shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from assumption of office.

questions.stem: Violations of Sections 7, 8 or 9 of RA 6713 are punishable by imprisonment not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Section 11(a) punishes violations of Sections 7, 8 or 9 with imprisonment not exceeding five (5) years, a fine not exceeding ₱5,000, or both, plus possible disqualification from public office.

questions.stem: Which agency has the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of RA 6713?
questions.explanation: Section 12 gives the Civil Service Commission the primary responsibility for the administration and enforcement of the Act.

questions.stem: Under RA 6713, a violation proven in a proper administrative proceeding is sufficient cause for removal or dismissal:
choices: even if no criminal prosecution is instituted
only if the official is elected
questions.explanation: Section 11(b) makes an administratively proven violation sufficient cause for removal or dismissal even if no criminal prosecution is instituted.

questions.stem: According to Article II of the 1987 Constitution, where does sovereignty reside?
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 1 declares the Philippines a democratic and republican State in which sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them.

questions.stem: The 1987 Constitution states that civilian authority is, at all times, supreme over the:
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 3 establishes civilian supremacy: civilian authority is, at all times, supreme over the military.

questions.stem: Under Article II, Section 2, the Philippines renounces war as:
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 2 states that the Philippines renounces war as an instrument of national policy and adopts the generally accepted principles of international law.

questions.stem: Which principle does Article II, Section 6 of the Constitution declare inviolable?
choices: The separation of Church and State
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 6 provides that the separation of Church and State shall be inviolable.

questions.stem: Article II, Section 27 directs the State to maintain honesty and integrity in the public service and to take positive and effective measures against:
questions.explanation: Section 27 of Article II commits the State to honesty and integrity in the public service and to positive and effective measures against graft and corruption.

questions.stem: Article II, Section 28 commits the State to a policy of full public disclosure of all its transactions involving:
questions.explanation: Subject to reasonable conditions prescribed by law, the State adopts and implements a policy of full public disclosure of all its transactions involving public interest.

questions.stem: Article II, Section 12 directs the State to equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from:
questions.explanation: Section 12 of Article II provides that the State shall equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception.

questions.stem: Article II, Section 14 of the Constitution directs the State to ensure the fundamental equality before the law of:
questions.explanation: Section 14 recognizes the role of women in nation-building and directs the State to ensure the fundamental equality before the law of women and men.

questions.stem: Under Article I, the waters around, between, and connecting the islands of the archipelago form part of the Philippines':
questions.explanation: Article I states that these waters, regardless of their breadth and dimensions, form part of the internal waters of the Philippines (the archipelagic doctrine).

questions.stem: In its Preamble, whose aid do the sovereign Filipino people implore?
questions.explanation: The Preamble begins: "We, the sovereign Filipino people, imploring the aid of Almighty God..."

questions.stem: Article III, Section 1 provides that no person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without:
questions.explanation: Section 1 of the Bill of Rights contains the due process and equal protection clauses.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 2, probable cause for issuing a search warrant or warrant of arrest must be determined personally by:
questions.explanation: No search warrant or warrant of arrest shall issue except upon probable cause to be determined personally by the judge after examining the complainant and witnesses under oath.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 3, evidence obtained in violation of the privacy of communication and correspondence is:
choices: admissible if a court later approves it
inadmissible for any purpose in any proceeding
questions.explanation: Section 3(2) of the Bill of Rights makes such evidence inadmissible for any purpose in any proceeding (the exclusionary rule).

questions.stem: Which right is protected by Article III, Section 4 of the Constitution?
choices: The right to a government job
The right to free college education
Freedom of speech, of expression, and of the press
questions.explanation: Section 4 provides that no law shall be passed abridging the freedom of speech, of expression, or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and petition the government for redress of grievances.

questions.stem: Article III, Section 7 recognizes the right of the people to information on matters of:
questions.explanation: Section 7 provides that the right of the people to information on matters of public concern shall be recognized, subject to limitations provided by law.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 9, private property shall not be taken for public use without:
questions.explanation: Section 9 limits the power of eminent domain: private property may be taken for public use only with just compensation.

questions.stem: Which of the following does Article III, Section 10 prohibit?
choices: A law impairing the obligation of contracts
questions.explanation: Section 10 states that no law impairing the obligation of contracts shall be passed.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 12, a person under investigation for an offense has the right to remain silent and to have competent and independent counsel preferably:
choices: from the Public Attorney's Office only
questions.explanation: Section 12 guarantees the right to remain silent and to competent and independent counsel preferably of the person's own choice (the Miranda rights).

questions.stem: Article III, Section 19 prohibits all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Imposing the death penalty without a law passed for compelling reasons involving heinous crimes
questions.explanation: Section 19(1) bars excessive fines and cruel, degrading or inhuman punishment, and bars the death penalty unless Congress provides for it for compelling reasons involving heinous crimes. Reasonable fines are not prohibited.

questions.stem: According to Article III, Section 20, no person shall be imprisoned for:
choices: debt or non-payment of a poll tax
questions.explanation: Section 20 provides that no person shall be imprisoned for debt or non-payment of a poll tax.

questions.stem: "No person shall be twice put in jeopardy of punishment for the same offense." This constitutional guarantee is known as the protection against:
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 21 protects against being tried or punished twice for the same offense, known as double jeopardy.

questions.stem: Article III, Section 22 prohibits the enactment of:
choices: ex post facto laws and bills of attainder
questions.explanation: Section 22 states that no ex post facto law or bill of attainder shall be enacted.

questions.stem: Under Article IV, natural-born citizens are those who are citizens of the Philippines from birth:
choices: after residing in the country for ten years
without having to perform any act to acquire or perfect their Philippine citizenship
after taking an oath of allegiance
only if both parents are Filipino
questions.explanation: Article IV, Section 2 defines natural-born citizens as those who are citizens from birth without having to perform any act to acquire or perfect their citizenship.

questions.stem: Under Article IV, Section 1, which of the following are citizens of the Philippines?
choices: Only those born on Philippine soil
Anyone who has lived in the Philippines for five years
Only those whose fathers are citizens
Those whose fathers or mothers are citizens of the Philippines
questions.explanation: Article IV, Section 1(2) includes those whose fathers or mothers are citizens of the Philippines. Citizenship follows blood (jus sanguinis), through either parent.

questions.stem: Under Article V, what is the minimum age to exercise the right of suffrage?
questions.explanation: Article V, Section 1 grants suffrage to citizens not otherwise disqualified by law who are at least eighteen years of age and meet the residence requirements.

questions.stem: To vote, a citizen must have resided in the Philippines for at least one year and in the place where they propose to vote for at least how long immediately preceding the election?
questions.explanation: Article V, Section 1 requires at least one year of residence in the Philippines and at least six months in the place where the voter proposes to vote.

questions.stem: Which requirement does Article V expressly forbid imposing on the exercise of suffrage?
questions.explanation: Article V, Section 1 provides that no literacy, property, or other substantive requirement shall be imposed on the exercise of suffrage.

questions.stem: How many Senators compose the Senate under the 1987 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 2 provides that the Senate shall be composed of twenty-four Senators elected at large.

questions.stem: What is the minimum age requirement for a Senator on the day of the election?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 3 requires a Senator to be at least thirty-five years of age on the day of the election.

questions.stem: A Senator may serve for no more than how many consecutive terms?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 4 provides that no Senator shall serve for more than two consecutive terms. A Senate term is six years.

questions.stem: What is the minimum age requirement for a Member of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 6 requires a Member of the House to be at least twenty-five years of age on the day of the election.

questions.stem: A Member of the House of Representatives may serve for no more than how many consecutive terms?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 7 limits House Members to three consecutive three-year terms.

questions.stem: Party-list representatives shall constitute what share of the total number of representatives, including those under the party list?
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 5(2) sets party-list representatives at twenty per centum of the total number of representatives.

questions.stem: Appropriation, revenue or tariff bills must originate exclusively in:
choices: the Department of Budget and Management
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 24 requires appropriation, revenue or tariff bills, among others, to originate exclusively in the House of Representatives, though the Senate may propose or concur with amendments.

questions.stem: Under Article VI, Section 26, every bill passed by Congress shall embrace:
choices: the approval of the President beforehand
only one subject, expressed in its title
questions.explanation: Section 26(1) of Article VI is the one-subject, one-title rule.

questions.stem: To declare the existence of a state of war, Congress must vote by:
choices: a simple majority of the Senate
two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately
three-fourths of all Members voting jointly
a majority of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 23(1) gives Congress the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war, by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately.

questions.stem: What is the minimum age requirement for President of the Philippines on the day of the election?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 2 requires the President to be at least forty years of age on the day of the election.

questions.stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, the President:
choices: may run again after a six-year gap
is not eligible for any re-election
may serve up to twelve years
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 4 provides that the President shall not be eligible for any re-election.

questions.stem: A Vice-President may serve for no more than how many successive terms?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 4 provides that no Vice-President shall serve for more than two successive terms.

questions.stem: The President may place the Philippines under martial law for a period not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 18 limits a proclamation of martial law or suspension of the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus to a period not exceeding sixty days, unless extended by Congress.

questions.stem: Within how many hours after proclaiming martial law must the President submit a report to Congress?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 18 requires the President to submit a report in person or in writing to Congress within forty-eight hours from the proclamation or suspension.

questions.stem: If both the President and Vice-President die, are permanently disabled, are removed, or resign, who shall act as President?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 8 provides that the President of the Senate or, in case of his inability, the Speaker of the House shall act as President until a President or Vice-President is elected and qualified.

questions.stem: The President's power to grant reprieves, commutations, and pardons does NOT extend to:
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 19 allows the President to grant reprieves, commutations, pardons and remit fines and forfeitures after conviction by final judgment, except in cases of impeachment.

questions.stem: For a treaty or international agreement to be valid and effective, it must be concurred in by at least:
choices: three-fourths of Congress in joint session
a majority of the House of Representatives
two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 21 requires the concurrence of at least two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court is composed of a Chief Justice and how many Associate Justices?
questions.explanation: Article VIII, Section 4(1) provides that the Supreme Court shall be composed of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices, fifteen members in all.

questions.stem: Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of:
questions.explanation: Article VIII, Section 11 provides that they hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of seventy years or become incapacitated.

questions.stem: Cases filed before the Supreme Court must be decided within how long from the date of submission?
questions.explanation: Article VIII, Section 15(1) sets twenty-four months for the Supreme Court, twelve months for lower collegiate courts, and three months for other lower courts.

questions.stem: The Judicial and Bar Council, which recommends appointees to the Judiciary, is under the supervision of:
choices: the Integrated Bar of the Philippines
questions.explanation: Article VIII, Section 8(1) creates the Judicial and Bar Council under the supervision of the Supreme Court.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the independent Constitutional Commissions?
questions.explanation: Article IX-A, Section 1 names only three independent Constitutional Commissions: the Civil Service Commission, the Commission on Elections, and the Commission on Audit. The Commission on Human Rights is created under Article XIII.

questions.stem: The Civil Service Commission is composed of:
choices: five Commissioners with a rotating Chair
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 1(1) provides that the civil service shall be administered by the Civil Service Commission composed of a Chairman and two Commissioners.

questions.stem: The civil service embraces all branches, subdivisions, instrumentalities, and agencies of the Government, including government-owned or controlled corporations:
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(1) includes GOCCs with original charters. GOCCs incorporated under the general corporation law are outside the civil service.

questions.stem: Appointments in the civil service shall be made only according to:
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(2) requires appointments according to merit and fitness, determined as far as practicable by competitive examination, with stated exceptions.

questions.stem: Competitive examination is generally required for civil service appointments, EXCEPT for positions that are:
choices: policy-determining, primarily confidential, or highly technical
clerical, custodial, or in the trades
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(2) exempts positions which are policy-determining, primarily confidential, or highly technical from the competitive-examination requirement.

questions.stem: Under the Constitution, an officer or employee of the civil service may be removed or suspended only:
choices: when the agency's budget is cut
upon the request of a superior
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(3) guarantees security of tenure: no officer or employee of the civil service shall be removed or suspended except for cause provided by law.

questions.stem: Civil service officers and employees are prohibited from engaging, directly or indirectly, in:
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(4) prohibits civil service officers and employees from engaging in any electioneering or partisan political campaign.

questions.stem: According to Article IX-B, the right to self-organization of government employees:
choices: requires CSC approval for each union
applies only to employees of GOCCs
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(5) states that the right to self-organization shall not be denied to government employees.

questions.stem: A candidate who lost in an election may NOT be appointed to any government office within what period after the election?
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 6 bars losing candidates from appointment to any office in the Government, or any GOCC or its subsidiaries, within one year after the election.

questions.stem: Unless specifically authorized by law, an elective or appointive public officer or employee may NOT receive:
choices: overtime pay approved by the agency
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 8 prohibits additional, double, or indirect compensation unless specifically authorized by law.

questions.stem: The Commission on Elections is composed of a Chairman and how many Commissioners?
questions.explanation: Article IX-C, Section 1(1) provides for a Chairman and six Commissioners. The CSC and COA each have a Chairman and two Commissioners.

questions.stem: For purposes of the three-term limit of local elective officials, voluntary renunciation of the office:
choices: is not considered an interruption in the continuity of service
resets the term count to zero
questions.explanation: Article X, Section 8 provides that voluntary renunciation of the office for any length of time shall not be considered an interruption in the continuity of service.

questions.stem: Article XI, Section 1 of the Constitution declares that public office is a:
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 1 states that public office is a public trust, and that public officers must at all times be accountable to the people.

questions.stem: Which of the following officials is NOT removable by impeachment?
choices: A Member of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 2 lists the impeachable officers: the President, the Vice-President, the Members of the Supreme Court, the Members of the Constitutional Commissions, and the Ombudsman.

questions.stem: Which body has the exclusive power to initiate all cases of impeachment?
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 3(1) gives the House of Representatives the exclusive power to initiate all cases of impeachment. The Senate tries and decides them.

questions.stem: Which body has the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment?
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 3(6) gives the Senate the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment.

questions.stem: No impeachment proceedings shall be initiated against the same official more than once within a period of:
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 3(5) bars initiating impeachment proceedings against the same official more than once within a period of one year.

questions.stem: Upon assumption of office, a public officer or employee must submit a declaration under oath of their:
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 17 requires a declaration under oath of assets, liabilities, and net worth upon assumption of office and as often as required by law, the basis of the SALN.

questions.stem: The Office of the Ombudsman is also known as the:
questions.explanation: Article XI, Section 5 creates the independent Office of the Ombudsman, to be known as the Tanodbayan.

questions.stem: Corporations allowed to enter into co-production, joint venture, or production-sharing agreements for natural resources must be at least what percent owned by Filipino citizens?
questions.explanation: Article XII, Section 2 refers to corporations or associations at least sixty per centum of whose capital is owned by Filipino citizens.

questions.stem: According to the Constitution, the national language of the Philippines is:
questions.explanation: Article XIV, Section 6 states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino. Filipino and English are the official languages (Section 7).

questions.stem: For purposes of communication and instruction, the official languages of the Philippines are:
choices: Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English
questions.explanation: Article XIV, Section 7 makes Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English the official languages. Regional languages are auxiliary official languages in the regions.

questions.stem: Under Article XIV, Section 5, the State shall assign the highest budgetary priority to:
questions.explanation: Article XIV, Section 5(5) directs the State to assign the highest budgetary priority to education.

questions.stem: According to the Constitution, the flag of the Philippines shall be red, white, and blue, with:
questions.explanation: Article XVI, Section 1 describes the flag as red, white, and blue, with a sun and three stars, as consecrated and honored by the people and recognized by law.

questions.stem: "The State may not be sued without its consent" expresses the doctrine of:
questions.explanation: Article XVI, Section 3 embodies the doctrine of state immunity: the State may not be sued without its consent.

questions.stem: Article XV, Section 1 recognizes which institution as the foundation of the nation?
questions.explanation: Article XV, Section 1 states that the State recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation.

questions.stem: Congress, acting as a constituent assembly, may propose amendments to the Constitution upon a vote of:
choices: a majority of all its Members
questions.explanation: Article XVII, Section 1 allows amendments or revisions to be proposed by Congress upon a vote of three-fourths of all its Members, or by a constitutional convention.

questions.stem: Amendments through people's initiative require a petition of at least what percentage of the total number of registered voters?
questions.explanation: Article XVII, Section 2 requires a petition of at least twelve per centum of all registered voters, with every legislative district represented by at least three per centum of its registered voters.

questions.stem: Under Article XIII, which body is created to investigate all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights?
choices: The Office of the Solicitor General
questions.explanation: Article XIII, Sections 17 and 18 create the independent Commission on Human Rights and empower it to investigate all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights.

questions.stem: Republic Act No. 9003 is known as the:
choices: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
questions.explanation: Section 1 of RA 9003 gives its short title as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.

questions.stem: Republic Act No. 8749 is known as the:
choices: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
questions.explanation: Section 1 of RA 8749 gives its short title as the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.

questions.stem: Republic Act No. 9275 is known as the:
choices: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
questions.explanation: Section 1 of RA 9275 gives its short title as the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004.

questions.stem: Republic Act No. 9729 is known as the:
questions.explanation: Section 1 of RA 9729 gives its title as the Climate Change Act of 2009.

questions.stem: Under RA 9003, within five years of the law's effectivity, each LGU must divert at least what share of its solid waste from disposal facilities through re-use, recycling and composting?
questions.explanation: Section 20 of RA 9003 requires each LGU to divert at least 25% of all solid waste from waste disposal facilities within five years, with targets increasing every three years after.

questions.stem: Under RA 9003, segregation of solid wastes shall primarily be conducted:
choices: at the materials recovery facility only
questions.explanation: Section 21 provides that segregation of wastes shall primarily be conducted at the source, including household, institutional, industrial, commercial and agricultural sources.

questions.stem: Under RA 9003, a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) shall be established in:
choices: every barangay or cluster of barangays
questions.explanation: Section 32 requires a Materials Recovery Facility in every barangay or cluster of barangays.

questions.stem: Under RA 9003, within how many years after the law's effectivity must every LGU convert its open dumps into controlled dumps?
questions.explanation: Section 37 prohibits open dumps and required every LGU to convert its open dumps into controlled dumps within three (3) years after the law took effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prohibited act under RA 9003?
choices: The open burning of solid waste
Bringing recyclables to a junk shop
questions.explanation: Section 48 of RA 9003 lists prohibited acts, including the open burning of solid waste and littering in public places.

questions.stem: Throwing or dumping waste matter in canals, esteros, sidewalks or parks is prohibited under which law?
questions.explanation: Section 48(1) of RA 9003 prohibits littering, throwing, dumping of waste matters in public places such as roads, sidewalks, canals, esteros or parks.

questions.stem: Under RA 9003, the National Solid Waste Management Commission is placed under:
choices: the Department of the Interior and Local Government
questions.explanation: Section 4 establishes the National Solid Waste Management Commission under the Office of the President.

questions.stem: RA 9003 defines composting as the controlled decomposition of organic matter by:
questions.explanation: Section 3(f) defines composting as the controlled decomposition of organic matter by micro-organisms, mainly bacteria and fungi, into a humus-like product.

questions.stem: RA 9003 defines an "open dump" as a disposal area where solid wastes are:
choices: indiscriminately thrown or disposed of without due planning
questions.explanation: Section 3(t) defines an open dump as a disposal area wherein solid wastes are indiscriminately thrown or disposed of without due planning and consideration for environmental and health standards.

questions.stem: The Clean Air Act defines incineration, which it bans, as the burning of:
choices: municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste that emits poisonous and toxic fumes
questions.explanation: Section 20 of RA 8749 bans incineration, defined as the burning of municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste which emits poisonous and toxic fumes, with exceptions such as traditional small-scale "siga" and crematoria.

questions.stem: Which of the following is EXEMPT from the Clean Air Act's ban on incineration?
choices: Burning of municipal garbage in a dumpsite
Burning of hospital waste in the open
questions.explanation: Section 20 of RA 8749 exempts the traditional small-scale "siga", traditional agricultural, cultural, health and food-preparation practices, and crematoria.

questions.stem: Under the Clean Air Act, smoking inside a public building or an enclosed public place, including public vehicles, is:
choices: prohibited, with implementation by the LGUs
questions.explanation: Section 24 of RA 8749 prohibits smoking inside public buildings, enclosed public places and public vehicles, outside designated areas, and assigns implementation to the LGUs.

questions.stem: Which right of citizens is the first listed under the Clean Air Act's recognition of rights?
choices: The right to free medical care
The right to breathe clean air
The right to own a vehicle
questions.explanation: Section 4(a) of RA 8749 recognizes the right to breathe clean air.

questions.stem: The Clean Air Act recognizes the principle that:
choices: the State shoulders all clean-up costs
questions.explanation: The declaration of policy of RA 8749 recognizes the principle that "polluters must pay".

questions.stem: Which agency is the lead agency for implementing and enforcing the Clean Air Act and the Clean Water Act?
choices: The Department of Public Works and Highways
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources
questions.explanation: Both laws make "the Department" (DENR) the primary government agency responsible for implementation and enforcement (RA 8749, Sec. 34; RA 9275, Sec. 19).

questions.stem: Under the Clean Water Act, water quality management areas are designated using physiographic units such as:
choices: watersheds, river basins or water resources regions
questions.explanation: Section 5 of RA 9275 designates water quality management areas using physiographic units such as watershed, river basins or water resources regions.

questions.stem: Under the Clean Water Act, "septage" refers to:
choices: sludge produced on individual onsite wastewater disposal systems such as septic tanks
questions.explanation: RA 9275 defines septage as the sludge produced on individual onsite wastewater disposal systems, principally septic tanks and cesspools.

questions.stem: Under the Clean Water Act, a person who pollutes water bodies beyond the applicable standards is responsible for:
choices: reporting it to the barangay only
containing, removing and cleaning up the pollution
nothing, if the pollution was accidental
questions.explanation: Section 16 of RA 9275 makes anyone who causes pollution in excess of standards responsible to contain, remove and clean up the pollution incident at their own expense.

questions.stem: Who serves as Chairperson of the Climate Change Commission under RA 9729?
choices: The Secretary of Science and Technology
The Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources
questions.explanation: Section 5 of RA 9729 makes the President of the Republic the Chairperson, with three Commissioners appointed by the President.

questions.stem: Under the Climate Change Act, which entities are the frontline agencies in formulating and implementing local climate change action plans?
questions.explanation: Section 14 of RA 9729 makes LGUs the frontline agencies in the formulation, planning and implementation of climate change action plans in their areas.

questions.stem: The Climate Change Act states that the State adopted which framework, espousing sustainable development?
questions.explanation: Section 2 of RA 9729 states that the State has adopted the Philippine Agenda 21 framework which espouses sustainable development.

questions.stem: According to Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, all human beings are born:
choices: subject to the laws of their country
free and equal in dignity and rights
questions.explanation: Article 1 of the UDHR states that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights, endowed with reason and conscience.

questions.stem: Article 3 of the UDHR guarantees everyone the right to:
choices: life, liberty and security of person
questions.explanation: Article 3 of the UDHR states that everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person.

questions.stem: Which UDHR article provides that no one shall be held in slavery or servitude?
questions.explanation: Article 4 states that no one shall be held in slavery or servitude, and that slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.

questions.stem: Under Article 5 of the UDHR, no one shall be subjected to:
choices: torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment
questions.explanation: Article 5 of the UDHR prohibits torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

questions.stem: Article 9 of the UDHR states that no one shall be subjected to arbitrary:
questions.explanation: Article 9 provides that no one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest, detention or exile.

questions.stem: Under Article 11 of the UDHR, everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be:
choices: presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial
tried by a jury of their choice
released on bail regardless of the offence
questions.explanation: Article 11 guarantees the presumption of innocence until proved guilty according to law in a public trial with all guarantees necessary for the defence.

questions.stem: Under Article 14 of the UDHR, everyone has the right to seek and to enjoy in other countries:
questions.explanation: Article 14 recognizes the right to seek and enjoy asylum from persecution, which cannot be invoked for genuinely non-political crimes.

questions.stem: Article 15 of the UDHR provides that everyone has the right to:
questions.explanation: Article 15 states that everyone has the right to a nationality and that no one shall be arbitrarily deprived of it.

questions.stem: According to Article 16 of the UDHR, marriage shall be entered into only with:
choices: the free and full consent of the intending spouses
questions.explanation: Article 16 requires the free and full consent of the intending spouses and calls the family the natural and fundamental group unit of society.

questions.stem: Under Article 20 of the UDHR, which statement is true about associations?
choices: No one may be compelled to belong to an association
Everyone must join at least one association
questions.explanation: Article 20 guarantees freedom of peaceful assembly and association, and states that no one may be compelled to belong to an association.

questions.stem: Article 21 of the UDHR recognizes everyone's right of equal access to:
questions.explanation: Article 21 states that everyone has the right of equal access to public service in his country, and that the will of the people is the basis of the authority of government.

questions.stem: Article 23 of the UDHR provides that everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to:
questions.explanation: Article 23 guarantees the right to work, to free choice of employment, and to equal pay for equal work, without discrimination.

questions.stem: Article 24 of the UDHR recognizes the right to rest and leisure, including:
choices: reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic holidays with pay
questions.explanation: Article 24 states that everyone has the right to rest and leisure, including reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic holidays with pay.

questions.stem: Under Article 26 of the UDHR, education shall be free at least in the:
questions.explanation: Article 26 provides that education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages, and that elementary education shall be compulsory.

questions.stem: According to Article 26 of the UDHR, who has a prior right to choose the kind of education given to their children?
questions.explanation: Article 26 states that parents have a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their children.

questions.stem: Article 29 of the UDHR states that, in exercising their rights and freedoms, everyone shall be subject only to limitations that are:
choices: determined by law to secure respect for the rights of others and meet just requirements of morality, public order and general welfare
questions.explanation: Article 29 allows only limitations determined by law solely to secure due recognition and respect for the rights and freedoms of others and to meet the just requirements of morality, public order and the general welfare in a democratic society.

questions.stem: Article 12 of the UDHR protects against arbitrary interference with a person's:
questions.explanation: Article 12 states that no one shall be subjected to arbitrary interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to attacks upon his honour and reputation.

questions.stem: Under Article 13 of the UDHR, everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to:
questions.explanation: Article 13 guarantees freedom of movement within a state and the right to leave any country, including one's own, and to return to one's country.

questions.stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, which body may investigate all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights, on its own or on complaint?
choices: The Department of Social Welfare and Development
questions.explanation: Article XIII, Section 18 empowers the Commission on Human Rights to investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights.

questions.stem: The 1987 Constitution provides that the State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees:
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 11 states that the State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees full respect for human rights.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 12(2) of the Constitution, which of the following is prohibited against a person under investigation?
choices: Being informed of the right to counsel
Torture, force, violence, threat or intimidation
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 12(2) states that no torture, force, violence, threat, intimidation, or any other means which vitiate the free will shall be used against such person.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 13 of the Constitution, the right to bail shall not be impaired even when:
choices: the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus is suspended
the accused is a public official
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 13 states that the right to bail shall not be impaired even when the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus is suspended.

questions.stem: Article III, Section 18 of the Constitution states that no person shall be detained solely by reason of his:
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 18(1) provides that no person shall be detained solely by reason of his political beliefs and aspirations.

questions.stem: Under Article III, Section 18(2), involuntary servitude in any form shall not exist EXCEPT as:
choices: a punishment for a crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 18(2) prohibits involuntary servitude except as punishment for a crime for which the party has been duly convicted.

questions.stem: Carlo is 4 years older than Tess. The sum of their ages is 68. How old is Carlo?
questions.explanation: Let Tess = x, so Carlo = x + 4. Then 2x + 4 = 68, x = 32, and Carlo is 32 + 4 = 36.

questions.stem: Tess is 3 times as old as Dina. In 11 years, Tess will be 2 times as old as Dina. How old is Tess now?
questions.explanation: Let Dina = x, so Tess = 3x. In 11 years: 3x + 11 = 2(x + 11). So x = 11, x = 11. Tess is 3 × 11 = 33.

questions.stem: Nina is 15 years older than Ana. The sum of their ages is 53. How old is Nina?
questions.explanation: Let Ana = x, so Nina = x + 15. Then 2x + 15 = 53, x = 19, and Nina is 19 + 15 = 34.

questions.stem: Dina is 4 years older than Liza. The sum of their ages is 54. How old is Dina?
questions.explanation: Let Liza = x, so Dina = x + 4. Then 2x + 4 = 54, x = 25, and Dina is 25 + 4 = 29.

questions.stem: Tess is 5 years older than Dina. The sum of their ages is 77. How old is Tess?
questions.explanation: Let Dina = x, so Tess = x + 5. Then 2x + 5 = 77, x = 36, and Tess is 36 + 5 = 41.

questions.stem: Liza is 7 years older than Joy. The sum of their ages is 59. How old is Liza?
questions.explanation: Let Joy = x, so Liza = x + 7. Then 2x + 7 = 59, x = 26, and Liza is 26 + 7 = 33.

questions.stem: Ana is 8 years older than Tess. The sum of their ages is 48. How old is Ana?
questions.explanation: Let Tess = x, so Ana = x + 8. Then 2x + 8 = 48, x = 20, and Ana is 20 + 8 = 28.

questions.stem: Nina is 4 years older than Paolo. The sum of their ages is 38. How old is Nina?
questions.explanation: Let Paolo = x, so Nina = x + 4. Then 2x + 4 = 38, x = 17, and Nina is 17 + 4 = 21.

questions.stem: Ben is 4 times as old as Ana. In 7 years, Ben will be 3 times as old as Ana. How old is Ben now?
questions.explanation: Let Ana = x, so Ben = 4x. In 7 years: 4x + 7 = 3(x + 7). So x = 14, x = 14. Ben is 4 × 14 = 56.

questions.stem: Tess is 2 years older than Carlo. The sum of their ages is 42. How old is Tess?
questions.explanation: Let Carlo = x, so Tess = x + 2. Then 2x + 2 = 42, x = 20, and Tess is 20 + 2 = 22.

questions.stem: Liza is 13 years older than Ana. The sum of their ages is 37. How old is Liza?
questions.explanation: Let Ana = x, so Liza = x + 13. Then 2x + 13 = 37, x = 12, and Liza is 12 + 13 = 25.

questions.stem: Ella is 6 times as old as Liza. In 2 years, Ella will be 4 times as old as Liza. How old is Ella now?
questions.explanation: Let Liza = x, so Ella = 6x. In 2 years: 6x + 2 = 4(x + 2). So 2x = 6, x = 3. Ella is 6 × 3 = 18.

questions.stem: Nina is 3 times as old as Ella. In 8 years, Nina will be 2 times as old as Ella. How old is Nina now?
questions.explanation: Let Ella = x, so Nina = 3x. In 8 years: 3x + 8 = 2(x + 8). So x = 8, x = 8. Nina is 3 × 8 = 24.

questions.stem: Rico is 3 times as old as Ben. In 6 years, Rico will be 2 times as old as Ben. How old is Rico now?
questions.explanation: Let Ben = x, so Rico = 3x. In 6 years: 3x + 6 = 2(x + 6). So x = 6, x = 6. Rico is 3 × 6 = 18.

questions.stem: Paolo is 13 years older than Vince. The sum of their ages is 87. How old is Paolo?
questions.explanation: Let Vince = x, so Paolo = x + 13. Then 2x + 13 = 87, x = 37, and Paolo is 37 + 13 = 50.

questions.stem: Mark is 8 years older than Rico. The sum of their ages is 20. How old is Mark?
questions.explanation: Let Rico = x, so Mark = x + 8. Then 2x + 8 = 20, x = 6, and Mark is 6 + 8 = 14.

questions.stem: Rico is 6 times as old as Joy. In 6 years, Rico will be 3 times as old as Joy. How old is Rico now?
questions.explanation: Let Joy = x, so Rico = 6x. In 6 years: 6x + 6 = 3(x + 6). So 3x = 12, x = 4. Rico is 6 × 4 = 24.

questions.stem: Ella is 5 times as old as Nina. In 6 years, Ella will be 3 times as old as Nina. How old is Ella now?
questions.explanation: Let Nina = x, so Ella = 5x. In 6 years: 5x + 6 = 3(x + 6). So 2x = 12, x = 6. Ella is 5 × 6 = 30.

questions.stem: Mark is 10 years older than Liza. The sum of their ages is 52. How old is Mark?
questions.explanation: Let Liza = x, so Mark = x + 10. Then 2x + 10 = 52, x = 21, and Mark is 21 + 10 = 31.

questions.stem: Liza is 4 years older than Paolo. The sum of their ages is 62. How old is Liza?
questions.explanation: Let Paolo = x, so Liza = x + 4. Then 2x + 4 = 62, x = 29, and Liza is 29 + 4 = 33.

questions.stem: Jun is 3 years older than Liza. The sum of their ages is 35. How old is Jun?
questions.explanation: Let Liza = x, so Jun = x + 3. Then 2x + 3 = 35, x = 16, and Jun is 16 + 3 = 19.

questions.stem: Paolo is 3 times as old as Liza. In 7 years, Paolo will be 2 times as old as Liza. How old is Paolo now?
questions.explanation: Let Liza = x, so Paolo = 3x. In 7 years: 3x + 7 = 2(x + 7). So x = 7, x = 7. Paolo is 3 × 7 = 21.

questions.stem: Carlo is 8 years older than Mark. The sum of their ages is 26. How old is Carlo?
questions.explanation: Let Mark = x, so Carlo = x + 8. Then 2x + 8 = 26, x = 9, and Carlo is 9 + 8 = 17.

questions.stem: Jun is 5 times as old as Ana. In 9 years, Jun will be 2 times as old as Ana. How old is Jun now?
questions.explanation: Let Ana = x, so Jun = 5x. In 9 years: 5x + 9 = 2(x + 9). So 3x = 9, x = 3. Jun is 5 × 3 = 15.

questions.stem: Dina is 3 times as old as Jun. In 14 years, Dina will be 2 times as old as Jun. How old is Dina now?
questions.explanation: Let Jun = x, so Dina = 3x. In 14 years: 3x + 14 = 2(x + 14). So x = 14, x = 14. Dina is 3 × 14 = 42.

questions.stem: Ella is 4 times as old as Joy. In 9 years, Ella will be 3 times as old as Joy. How old is Ella now?
questions.explanation: Let Joy = x, so Ella = 4x. In 9 years: 4x + 9 = 3(x + 9). So x = 18, x = 18. Ella is 4 × 18 = 72.

questions.stem: Joy is 2 years older than Jun. The sum of their ages is 80. How old is Joy?
questions.explanation: Let Jun = x, so Joy = x + 2. Then 2x + 2 = 80, x = 39, and Joy is 39 + 2 = 41.

questions.stem: Jun is 3 years older than Dina. The sum of their ages is 25. How old is Jun?
questions.explanation: Let Dina = x, so Jun = x + 3. Then 2x + 3 = 25, x = 11, and Jun is 11 + 3 = 14.

questions.stem: Tess is 5 times as old as Liza. In 10 years, Tess will be 3 times as old as Liza. How old is Tess now?
questions.explanation: Let Liza = x, so Tess = 5x. In 10 years: 5x + 10 = 3(x + 10). So 2x = 20, x = 10. Tess is 5 × 10 = 50.

questions.stem: Tess is 4 times as old as Rico. In 7 years, Tess will be 3 times as old as Rico. How old is Tess now?
questions.explanation: Let Rico = x, so Tess = 4x. In 7 years: 4x + 7 = 3(x + 7). So x = 14, x = 14. Tess is 4 × 14 = 56.

questions.stem: Vince is 15 years older than Carlo. The sum of their ages is 87. How old is Vince?
questions.explanation: Let Carlo = x, so Vince = x + 15. Then 2x + 15 = 87, x = 36, and Vince is 36 + 15 = 51.

questions.stem: Ben is 4 times as old as Ana. In 3 years, Ben will be 3 times as old as Ana. How old is Ben now?
questions.explanation: Let Ana = x, so Ben = 4x. In 3 years: 4x + 3 = 3(x + 3). So x = 6, x = 6. Ben is 4 × 6 = 24.

Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Each of the applicants ___ required to submit a birth certificate.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is", even when followed by a plural phrase like "of the applicants".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The list of requirements ___ posted on the bulletin board.
questions.explanation: The subject is "list" (singular), not "requirements". A singular subject takes the singular verb "is".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ aware of the new memo.
questions.explanation: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Clerks" is plural, so the verb is "were".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The director, along with her two assistants, ___ attending the seminar.
questions.explanation: Phrases like "along with" do not change the number of the subject. "The director" is singular, so the verb is "is".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The documents were given to Maria and ___.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to", use the object pronoun "me". Test it by dropping "Maria and": "given to me".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Between you and ___, the report is not yet finished.
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes object pronouns: "between you and me".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
She is the employee ___ received the service award.
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of the verb "received". Use "whom" only for objects, and "which" for things, not people.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
To ___ should the complaint be addressed?
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to", the object form "whom" is required.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The office will be closed ___ Monday because of the holiday.
questions.explanation: Use "on" with specific days and dates (on Monday, on June 12), "in" with months and years, and "at" with clock times.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The seminar starts ___ 8:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Use "at" for specific clock times.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
By the time the inspector arrived, the workers ___ the site.
questions.explanation: The past perfect "had left" shows an action completed before another past action (the inspector's arrival).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
If I ___ the head of the agency, I would simplify the process.
questions.explanation: Hypothetical or contrary-to-fact conditions use the subjunctive "were" for all subjects: "If I were...".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The new procedure will ___ the waiting time of clients.
questions.explanation: "Affect" is usually the verb meaning to influence; "effect" is usually the noun meaning a result.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The agency posted ___ new Citizen's Charter at the entrance.
questions.explanation: "Its" is the possessive form, which is needed here. "It's" means "it is" or "it has", and "its'" is never correct.

questions.stem:

The applicants left ___ folders at the reception desk.
questions.explanation: "Their" is the possessive form. "There" refers to a place, and "they're" means "they are".

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: Use "fewer" with countable nouns (complaints) and "less" with uncountable nouns (less time, less water).

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: When comparing exactly two things, use the comparative form "better". "Best" is for three or more.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: "The number of..." is singular and takes "has". By contrast, "a number of applicants" means several applicants and takes a plural verb.

questions.explanation: A third-person singular subject takes "doesn't" followed by the base form of the verb: "She doesn't know".

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The clerk, who was new, made several errors.
The clerk who was new, made several errors.
The clerk, who was new made several errors.
The clerk who, was new, made several errors.
questions.explanation: A non-essential clause is set off by a pair of commas, one before and one after: "The clerk, who was new, made several errors."

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Walking to the office, I saw a long line of applicants.
Walking to the office, a long line of applicants was seen.
Walking to the office, the applicants' line was long.
A long line of applicants, walking to the office, I saw.
questions.explanation: An introductory participle phrase must describe the subject that follows it. Only "I" can be the one walking; the other options are dangling modifiers.

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

Neither of the two offices are open on Sunday.
Neither of the two office is open on Sunday.
Neither of the two offices were open on Sunday.
questions.explanation: "Neither" used as a pronoun is singular and takes "is".

The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quick and accurate.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quickly and accurate.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quick and accurately.
questions.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs. Both "quickly" and "accurately" describe how to complete, and parallel structure needs both in adverb form.

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The applicants were asked to bring a pen, a photo, and an ID.
The applicants were asked to bring a pen, a photo, and ID's.
The applicants were asked to bringing a pen, a photo, and an ID.
The applicants was asked to bring a pen, a photo, and an ID.
questions.explanation: Plural subject "applicants" takes "were". "To" is followed by the base verb "bring", and the list items are parallel.

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The new employees (A) has been (B) assigned to (C) the records section (D).
questions.explanation: The plural subject "employees" needs the plural verb "have been", not "has been".

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
My colleague and me (A) were sent (B) to the regional office (C) last week (D).
questions.explanation: The subject needs the subject pronoun: "My colleague and I were sent...".

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The report must be submitted (A) by Friday, (B) irregardless of (C) the delay in data gathering (D).
questions.explanation: "Irregardless" is nonstandard. Use "regardless of".

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The supervisor (A) gave the instructions (B) to Ana and I (C) this morning (D).
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to", use the object pronoun: "to Ana and me". Test it by dropping "Ana and": "to me".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The staff were told to ___ their reports before the deadline.
questions.explanation: After "to", use the base form of the verb: "to proofread".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The chairman insisted that every member ___ present at the hearing.
questions.explanation: Verbs of demand or insistence take the subjunctive base form: "insisted that every member be present".

Read the passage, then answer the question.

The town of San Rafael once struggled with garbage piling up along its creek. Instead of buying more trucks, the municipal government trained household volunteers to separate biodegradable waste from recyclables. Within a year, the volume of garbage sent to the dumpsite fell by almost half, and the money saved was used to build a small composting facility.

What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Composting facilities are expensive to build.
The creek in San Rafael is now completely clean.
Training households to segregate waste reduced garbage and saved money.
San Rafael bought more garbage trucks to clean its creek.
questions.explanation: The passage describes how household segregation, rather than more trucks, cut garbage nearly in half and freed funds for composting. The passage never says the creek is completely clean.

According to the passage, how was the money saved used?
choices: To build a small composting facility
questions.explanation: The last sentence states that the money saved was used to build a small composting facility.

Which can be inferred from the passage?
choices: The town's earlier approach to garbage was less effective than involving households.
The dumpsite has been permanently closed.
The volunteers were paid a monthly salary.
Other towns have copied San Rafael's program.
questions.explanation: The contrast between the old problem and the result after involving households implies the earlier approach worked less well. The other choices add facts the passage never gives.

questions.stem:

Many government offices now post a Citizen's Charter at their entrance. The charter lists each service the office provides, the documents required, the steps to follow, the fees, and the maximum time each step should take. By making these standards public, the charter allows clients to know what to expect and gives them a basis for complaining when service falls short.

According to the passage, which of the following is NOT listed in a Citizen's Charter?
choices: The maximum time for each step
The names of employees who were disciplined
questions.explanation: The passage lists services, required documents, steps, fees, and maximum processing times. It says nothing about disciplined employees.

What is the purpose of making service standards public, according to the passage?
choices: So clients know what to expect and can complain when service falls short
So offices can charge higher fees
So the office does not need to answer questions
So employees can work fewer hours
questions.explanation: The final sentence gives both purposes: clients know what to expect and have a basis for complaints.

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Mangrove forests protect coastal communities in ways that are easy to overlook. Their tangled roots slow down waves and reduce the force of storm surges, while also trapping soil that would otherwise wash into the sea. The roots also shelter young fish and crabs, so fishermen who live near healthy mangroves often enjoy better catches. Despite this, many mangrove areas have been cleared for fishponds and housing.

Which title best fits the passage?
choices: The Dangers of Fishing at Sea
questions.explanation: The passage explains several hidden benefits of mangroves (storm protection, soil retention, fish nurseries) and notes they are still being cleared.

According to the passage, why do fishermen near healthy mangroves often have better catches?
choices: Storm surges bring in more fish.
The roots shelter young fish and crabs.
questions.explanation: The passage states that the roots shelter young fish and crabs, which leads to better catches.

When the provincial hospital introduced an online appointment system, older patients at first complained that they did not know how to use it. The hospital responded by keeping two walk-in windows open and assigning volunteers to help patients book on their phones. After six months, waiting times had dropped and complaints had nearly disappeared.

How did the hospital respond to the older patients' complaints?
choices: It required all patients to book online.
It cancelled the online appointment system.
It kept walk-in windows open and assigned volunteers to help with booking.
questions.explanation: The second sentence describes the response: two walk-in windows stayed open and volunteers helped patients book.
