When the provincial hospital introduced an online appointment system, older patients at first complained that they did not know how to use it. The hospital responded by keeping two walk-in windows open and assigning volunteers to help patients book on their phones. After six months, waiting times had dropped and complaints had nearly disappeared.

Which lesson is best supported by the passage?
choices: New systems work better when users who struggle with them are given support.
Walk-in windows are always faster than online booking.
Online systems should never be used in hospitals.
Older patients refuse to learn new technology.
questions.explanation: The passage shows that the system succeeded once struggling users got help and an alternative. The other choices overgeneralize or contradict the passage.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word.
The clerk was DILIGENT in sorting the applications.
questions.explanation: Diligent means showing steady, careful effort, so hardworking is the closest meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The instructions were AMBIGUOUS, so many applicants filled out the form incorrectly.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation, or unclear. That explains why applicants made mistakes.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The agency issued a TEMPORARY permit while the main application was processed.
questions.explanation: Temporary means lasting for a limited time. Provisional means arranged for the present, possibly to be changed later.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The official tried to MITIGATE the effects of the flood on the evacuees.
questions.explanation: To mitigate is to make something less severe, so lessen is the closest meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
Her CANDID remarks during the meeting surprised the panel.
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward, or frank. Rude adds an insult that candid does not carry.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The new policy will SUPERSEDE the old guidelines.
questions.explanation: To supersede is to take the place of something older, so replace is the closest meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The report was so VERBOSE that the main point was hard to find.
questions.explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed, or wordy.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The barangay captain was known for his PRUDENT use of funds.
questions.explanation: Prudent means acting with care and good judgment, especially about the future, so careful is the closest meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The office has an ADEQUATE supply of forms for the month.
questions.explanation: Adequate means enough for a requirement, or sufficient.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The witness gave a LUCID account of the incident.
questions.explanation: Lucid means expressed clearly and easy to understand.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The committee was criticized for its PERFUNCTORY review of the complaints.
questions.explanation: Perfunctory describes something done only as a routine duty, with little care or effort. Superficial is the closest meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The two agencies decided to COLLABORATE on the vaccination drive.
questions.explanation: To collaborate is to work jointly with others, or to cooperate.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The mayor's speech was full of ERUDITE references to history.
questions.explanation: Erudite means having or showing great knowledge or learning, so scholarly is the closest meaning.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The employee was COMMENDED for returning the lost wallet.
questions.explanation: To commend is to praise formally or officially.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The road project was put on hold due to INSUFFICIENT funds.
questions.explanation: Insufficient means not enough, or inadequate. Missing would mean entirely absent.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The auditor found the explanation SPECIOUS and asked for supporting documents.
questions.explanation: Specious means seeming reasonable or true on the surface but actually wrong, or misleadingly plausible.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The residents were RELUCTANT to leave their homes despite the warning.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling and hesitant. Unable would mean they lacked the ability, which is a different idea.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
Please VERIFY the applicant's documents before approval.
questions.explanation: To verify is to make sure something is true or accurate, or to confirm.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The official remained IMPARTIAL throughout the hearing.
questions.explanation: Impartial means treating all sides equally, without bias, or neutral.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The typhoon caused EXTENSIVE damage to crops in the region.
questions.explanation: Extensive means covering a large area or wide range, or widespread.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The director's EPHEMERAL popularity faded after a few months.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, which matches popularity that faded within months.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The teacher's EXPLICIT instructions left no room for confusion.
questions.explanation: Explicit means stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The new system made the processing of permits more EFFICIENT.
questions.explanation: Efficient means achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The spokesperson gave an EQUIVOCAL answer to avoid committing to a date.
questions.explanation: Equivocal means open to more than one interpretation, often deliberately vague. An evasive answer avoids committing, as described.

questions.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the capitalized word.
The newly hired staff were ENTHUSIASTIC about their first assignment.
questions.explanation: Enthusiastic means showing intense and eager enjoyment or interest.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The line at the cashier was moving at a RAPID pace.
questions.explanation: Rapid means fast; its opposite is slow. Quick is a synonym, not an antonym.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The hall was CROWDED during the job fair.
questions.explanation: Crowded means full of people; its opposite is empty.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The supervisor's response to the complaint was HOSTILE.
questions.explanation: Hostile means unfriendly or antagonistic; its opposite is friendly.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The committee gave its UNANIMOUS approval.
questions.explanation: Unanimous means fully agreed by everyone; the opposite is divided.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The city's budget showed a large DEFICIT this year.
questions.explanation: A deficit is an amount by which spending exceeds income; its opposite is a surplus. Loss, debt and shortage are all close in meaning to deficit.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The new procedure is VOLUNTARY for all employees.
questions.explanation: Voluntary means done by choice; its opposite is compulsory, meaning required.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The officer gave a VAGUE description of the suspect.
questions.explanation: Vague means unclear or imprecise; its opposite is precise.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
His FRUGAL habits helped him save for a house.
questions.explanation: Frugal means sparing or economical with money; its opposite is extravagant. Thrifty is a synonym.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The evidence against the accused was CONCLUSIVE.
questions.explanation: Conclusive means settling an issue decisively; its opposite is inconclusive. The other choices are near-synonyms.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The speaker's tone was CONCILIATORY.
questions.explanation: Conciliatory means intended to calm or make peace; its opposite is antagonistic.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The client's request was ACCEPTED by the office.
questions.explanation: Accepted is the opposite of rejected.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The weather in the mountains is usually MILD in December.
questions.explanation: Mild weather is gentle and not extreme; the opposite is harsh.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The plan was criticized as being too RIGID.
questions.explanation: Rigid means unable to bend or change; its opposite is flexible.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The population of the town has been INCREASING.
questions.explanation: Increasing means growing; its opposite is declining. Stable means neither increasing nor decreasing, so it is not the opposite.

questions.stem:
Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word.
The witness was RETICENT when asked about the incident.
questions.explanation: Reticent means not revealing one's thoughts readily; its opposite is talkative. Reserved is a synonym.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
PEN : WRITE :: KNIFE : ___
questions.explanation: A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut. The relationship is tool to function.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
DOCTOR : HOSPITAL :: TEACHER : ___
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school. The relationship is worker to workplace.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
PUPPY : DOG :: KITTEN : ___
questions.explanation: A puppy is a young dog; a kitten is a young cat.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
HOT : COLD :: ANCIENT : ___
questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites; the opposite of ancient is modern.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
PAGE : BOOK :: BRICK : ___
questions.explanation: A page is a part of a book; a brick is a part of a wall. The relationship is part to whole.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
THERMOMETER : TEMPERATURE :: ODOMETER : ___
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; an odometer measures distance traveled. A speedometer measures speed.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
AUTHOR : NOVEL :: COMPOSER : ___
questions.explanation: An author creates a novel; a composer creates a symphony. The relationship is creator to creation.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
DROUGHT : WATER :: FAMINE : ___
questions.explanation: A drought is a severe shortage of water; a famine is a severe shortage of food. Hunger is a result of famine, not the thing lacking.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
FINGER : HAND :: TOE : ___
questions.explanation: A finger is part of a hand; a toe is part of a foot.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
BENEVOLENT : KIND :: MALEVOLENT : ___
questions.explanation: Benevolent means kind; malevolent means wishing harm, or wicked. Each pair is word to synonym.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
CAPTAIN : SHIP :: PILOT : ___
questions.explanation: A captain commands a ship; a pilot flies an airplane. The relationship is operator to vehicle.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
SCARCE : ABUNDANT :: TIMID : ___
questions.explanation: Scarce and abundant are opposites; the opposite of timid is bold.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
SEED : TREE :: EGG : ___
questions.explanation: A seed grows into a tree; an egg develops into a bird. The relationship is beginning stage to mature form.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
LIBRARIAN : BOOKS :: CURATOR : ___
questions.explanation: A librarian manages and cares for books; a curator manages and cares for a collection of artifacts or exhibits, as in a museum.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
HUNGRY : EAT :: TIRED : ___
questions.explanation: When hungry, one eats to satisfy the need; when tired, one rests. Yawning is a symptom of tiredness, not what relieves it.
